newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Teva is most active Tel Aviv share.
newsitem.headline: Teva is most active Tel Aviv share.

text.p: Teva Pharmaceutical Industries was the most actively traded share on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE) in 1996, the fifth year in a row it has led the list, the stock exchange said on Wednesday.

However, Teva's American depositary receipts (ADRs), which trade on the Nasdaq, were more heavily traded, the TASE said. The equivalent of nine billion shekels in Teva was traded over 1996 in the United States, seven times the 1.319 billion shekels in Tel Aviv.

Koor Industries was a close second in volume, with 1.268 billion shekels in shares changing hands last year. Bezeq was number three, with an annual turnover of 892 million shekels and Bank Hapoalim fourth with 782 million shekels.
The TASE said the top 20 traded shares accounted for 46 percent on the exchange's total turnover in 1996, or 10.258 billion shekels. That was up from 39 percent in 1995 and 31 percent in 1994.
The exchange attributed the increase to reduced trading in smaller, less liquid stocks over the last three years.

IDB Holdings jumped to fifth from 10th place because of heavy trading during a competition for control of the company between the Recanti family and industrialist Stef Wertheimer in June 1996. Tadiran Ltd rose to 10th place from 16th.
The TASE noted that seven of the top 20 companies were also traded in the United States.
